data.name: Mahish
data.gender_notes: Mahish is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Mahish is the name of a demon in the form of a buffalo or a bull. He was slain by the goddess Durga in her form as Mahishasura Mardini. The name Mahish carries the meaning “Buffalo Demon” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Mahish usually hope their child will grow to embody buffalo demon and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Mahish belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Buffalo Demon.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mahish total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Mahish is deeply rooted in Hindu mythology and symbolizes power, strength, and fearlessness. This name has cultural significance as it represents the victory of good over evil. The tale of Mahishasura and Durga is an iconic representation of feminine power and the triumph of the divine protectress over a powerful demon. This story also highlights the importance of courage, determination, loyalty, and unwavering faith.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, the name Mahish holds deep spiritual significance as it represents the ultimate victory of truth and good over evil and ignorance. It serves as a reminder that no matter the size or strength of the challenge, one can overcome it with the power of self-belief, resilience, and loyalty to the divine. Additionally, it highlights the feminine divine through the image of Durga, who is depicted as the fierce protector and nurturer of her children. The name Mahish also underscores the importance of uncompromising devotion to one's deity and the belief that absolute surrender to the divine will lead to salvation and ultimate enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Mahish represents the embodiment of evil and ignorance, symbolized by the Buffalo demon. It is a reminder of the power of fear and darkness that resides within us, encouraging us to face and overcome our inner demons.

vedic_reference.note: Mahisha-asura, a demon king in Hindu mythology, who was slain by Goddess Durga. He is depicted as a mighty bull-demon and is known for his immense strength and invincibility.

historical_references.reference:
Mahishasura, a demon king, was a powerful asura who terrorized the gods and goddesses in Hindu mythology. He was born from the demon mother Mahishasur Mardini, when she was granted a boon by Lord Brahma that she could not be defeated by a god or a man. Mahishasura terrorized the heavens and gods for a long time, eventually being slain by the goddess Durga in a fierce battle.
Time period: Unknown, likely pre-Mauryan period.
Context: Hindu mythology, Puranic literature

Mahisha, also known as Mahishasura or Mahisha, was the king of demons and a powerful asura in Hindu mythology. He is said to have been the son of the demon king Vrisha and is mentioned in several ancient Hindu texts, including the Mahabharata and the Ramayana.
Time period: Around 800-500 BCE.
Context: Hindu mythology, ancient Indian literature
